A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, with the same title, authors, and core Information Imbalance analysis. All 23 pages of v4 and 18 pages of v5, including their equations, figures, and appendices, support comparison despite extensive restructuring.

before.justification: V4 reports original Gaussian simulations and empirical analyses of multilingual text, same-class images, and image-caption representations, including supplementary experiments.

after.justification: V5 reports original simulations and representation analyses, including language and model asymmetries, token aggregation experiments, and visual-model comparisons.

M1.justification: The rank-based Information Imbalance estimator remains mathematically unchanged. The adopted representation pipeline changes from concatenated tokens in v4's main analyses to token averaging in v5's subsequent analyses (Section 2.1). Averaging was already tested in v4's appendices, so this is an adaptation of the existing pipeline rather than a new algorithm.

E1.justification: Opus Books, ImageNet-1k, and Flickr30k remain the principal datasets. Translation coverage becomes English-centered, adds French and Dutch, and drops the Spanish-Italian and German-Hungarian pairings. V5 also adds an alignment scenario comparing different models processing identical English inputs.

E2.justification: Neighborhood Overlap joins the synthetic II/CKA comparisons, and CKA joins the translation comparison previously conducted with II and Neighborhood Overlap. BERT disappears from the translation model comparison. The earlier CLIP comparisons with DeepSeek-V3 and DinoV2 are replaced by CLIP-Image versus CLIP-Text, while image-caption comparisons add Llama3.1-8B and DinoV2-base/small.

E3.justification: Besides changing token aggregation, v5 changes translation sample counts from approximately 5,000 to 1,000–3,000 and ImageNet pair counts from 2,500 to 1,000. The main image-caption experiment fixes DeepSeek-V3 near 60% depth instead of layer 52. Synthetic feature dimensions change from 1,000/100,000 to 100/10,000. These are revised reported settings, not merely additional disclosure.

E4.justification: V5 extends directional comparisons across languages and models, reworks token aggregation and correlation analyses, and adds vision-model-size and fixed-layer controls. It removes v4's longer-sentence experiment, binarization check, intrinsic-dimension analysis, BERT forward/backward analysis, and image-token-window sensitivity studies. The shuffled-translation control is retained, moving from v4 Appendix E to v5 Appendix A.

E5.justification: Several text-analysis captions change from five subsamples of 2,000 out of 5,000 to five half-dataset subsamples; synthetic benchmarks retain ten jackknife repetitions. V5's vision plots retain shaded bands but omit v4's explicit image-pair repetition counts, bootstrap procedure, and CLIP 95% confidence-interval definition. These are reporting and resampling changes, without evidence of increased run counts.

E6.justification: Results are substantially replaced or added under changed settings. DinoV2's same-class-image minimum changes from approximately 0.43 to 0.35, and its cross-modal asymmetry changes from favoring the visual representation to favoring DeepSeek-V3. New CLIP-pair and model-size results are reported. Exact values in v5 are internally inconsistent: Section 3.2.2 quotes approximately 0.20 for DeepSeek-V3 to DinoV2, whereas Figure 6b plots a minimum near 0.10. These changes cannot be treated as same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The principal Information Imbalance definition is retained in equivalent notation. V4 Appendix H's formal Binary Intrinsic Dimension probability model, ansatz, and divergence-based fitting formulation are removed. No replacement theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The semantic-layer and distributed-token claims remain, but v5 adds prominent claims about English's directional advantage, DeepSeek-V3 predicting smaller models better than the reverse, and model scale potentially outweighing joint multimodal training. Its independent-model-versus-CLIP claim uses a different comparison from v4's claim that CLIP's visual encoder improves alignment with DeepSeek-V3.

C2.justification: V5 adds interpretations involving central-layer symmetry, language-dependent early and late asymmetries, vision-model capacity saturation, and low-frequency semantic encoding. It attributes CLIP's more symmetric alignment to joint training. V4's specific qualifications about different novels confounding language comparisons and biases from model-generated translations disappear, although v5 acknowledges unresolved effects of model size, training regime, and modality.

D1.justification: Sentence filtering details move into v5 Section 2.2 and remain available. However, v5 removes v4's hardware, memory, and SGLang disclosures, asset and checkpoint access list, explicit distance/preprocessing details, and future code-release statement. It newly specifies the synthetic sample size and language-selection rationale, but overall reproducibility documentation is substantially reduced.

R1.justification: The central positioning around the Platonic Representation Hypothesis and Information Imbalance remains. V5 adds connections to metric criticism, cross-lingual retrieval, token-trajectory geometry, and frequency-based representations, citing Gröger et al., Liu and Niehues, Hosseini and Fedorenko, and Tamkin et al. Quantization and intrinsic-dimension background citations are removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, methods, and conclusion undergo extensive rewriting. Methods are reorganized around representation choice, data/models, and the statistic; results foreground aggregation and directional asymmetries. The standalone limitations, ethics, and reproducibility sections disappear, and the supplementary material is substantially reorganized.

P2.justification: Many figures are redrawn and regrouped: the synthetic benchmark becomes three panels, aggregation and asymmetry receive dedicated displays, token correlations use four model-language panels with depth coloring, and the main vision figure incorporates CLIP. Supplementary plots are removed or replaced, with substantial changes to legends, axes, figure sizing, and page layout beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: V5 offers clearer organization and useful additional evidence about directional predictability, aggregation, and model scale. However, it removes substantial reproducibility and uncertainty documentation supplied by v4, while its central image-caption numerical discussion disagrees with the plotted results, notably in Figure 6b. The intended quantitative values and their uncertainty remain unresolved, preventing a reliable net quality judgment against the benefits of the added analyses.
